label: D2 a2->S2 common after an unrewarded a2 trial, growing steeply late in episode
explanation: Fires only at D2. Its size is set by a conjunction: this trial a2 reached S2 (common), the previous trial was also a2 and went unrewarded (after a2 S1 u or a2 S2 u), and the episode is late. Within that context it grows roughly linearly from trial 50, and the ep_trial>75 hinge term adjusts the slope of that growth. Its magnitude is also graded by the policy logit at D2 (fitted weight negative, so larger when the policy leans toward a2). It is about 0 at D1 and GO, after a1 trials, after rewarded trials, and on rare a2->S1 trials. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.49 with 3 terms (the single conjunction x max(ep_trial-50,0) term alone gets 0.42), well above the additive all-cue ceiling of 0.18. Adding the value output, reward two or three trials back, or whether the last state was S1 vs S2 added little. The model still under-predicts the largest peaks (about 1.9 actual vs about 0.5 predicted), which often come after several unrewarded trials in a row, but terms for earlier rewards did not capture this. Uses no future variables; choice is the model policy output.

issues: The ep_trial>75 hinge does nothing on test. Dropping it leaves R^2 beyond timing at 0.4854, against 0.4856 with all 3 terms. The two-term model of ramp plus ramp*choice gives 0.4854; ramp plus hinge gives 0.4196, against 0.4191 for the ramp alone. The claim that the hinge 'adjusts the slope' is unsupported. All of the gain beyond the single term comes from the choice interaction.

There is a systematic miss caused by how the conjunction is coded. prev_action==2 is false on each window's first trial, where prev_action = -1 (unknown), so peaks there are predicted as about 0. The worst-fit dev window is one of these: [-3 t83] S2c, actual 2.05, predicted 0.06. Replacing prev_action==2 with prev_action!=1 raises test R^2 from 0.486 to 0.596 with only 2 terms. The residual table shows the feature is about 0 after a1 trials (about -0.018), so prev_action==-1 rows here are effectively prior-a2 cases.

Large peaks are still under-predicted even with the fix: about 1.9-2.05 actual against about 0.42-0.52 predicted in all the top dev misfits. Activations look bimodal (about 0.3-0.7 versus about 1.9) at similar ep_trial. A streak of 2-3 unrewarded a2 trials adds only about 0.003 R^2 (0.489). Value, the good state, and nonlinear choice or ramp shapes add at most about 0.017 (best 0.613). The cause of the peaks is still unidentified, so the 'several unrewarded trials in a row' remark is anecdotal.

Claims that do check out: activation is exactly 0 at D1 and GO; on D2 the residual is about -0.018 after a1 trials and after rewarded trials, and -0.019 on rare a2->S1 trials; it is positive after a2 S2 u (+0.057) and a2 S1 u (+0.091). The choice weight is negative, so the feature is larger when the logit leans toward a2. No future variables are used.

Minor point: the previous unrewarded a2 trial pays slightly more after a rare S1 outcome than after a common S2 one (residuals +0.091 vs +0.057). A prev_state==1 term adds only 0.006 on test (0.491), though.
